# AI Policy File

> Free eight-question educational screener that helps creators and small
> businesses identify five AI-disclosure frameworks that may warrant review.
> It provides source-based explanations and official links; it does not decide
> jurisdiction, coverage, compliance, or legal duties.

## Frameworks covered (reviewed August 2, 2026)

- FTC Endorsement Guides and Section 5 (United States; material connections,
  truthful endorsements, and deceptive advertising, not a general AI-use label)
- EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations (generally applicable August 2,
  2026; a narrow transition to December 2, 2026 applies only to Article 50(2)
  systems placed on the market before August 2, 2026)
- New York Synthetic Performer Disclosure Law S.8420-A (effective June 9, 2026)
- California B.O.T. Act SB 1001 (in force since July 1, 2019)
- California AI Transparency Act (SB 942 as amended by AB 853): the chapter
  and covered-provider duties became operative August 2, 2026; added
  large-online-platform and GenAI-hosting duties begin January 1, 2027, and
  capture-device-manufacturer duties begin January 1, 2028. Pending SB 1000
  is not current law as of this review.

## Important checker limit

The eight-question checker does not screen emotion-recognition or
biometric-categorisation systems under EU AI Act Article 50(3). Users who
provide or deploy either category should review that provision separately.
Its final California question groups covered providers, affected third-party
licensees, large online platforms, GenAI hosting platforms, and capture device
manufacturers, whose definitions, conditions, and operative dates differ. The
official code controls.
